consensus_findings.description: Critical: A first projection generation inserted after an SSE client connects emits no refresh event. Migration 038 inserts the canonical row with both owned labels already present, but migration 037 installs `trg_work_queue_notify` as `AFTER UPDATE` only and `notify_work_queue_change` emits `projection.labels_changed` only when OLD and NEW labels differ. With no stale row and no conflict, the initial submit performs no UPDATE, so `event_stream.py` never builds a fresh snapshot and the connected board remains stale until unrelated traffic or polling. The live SSE test starts from an already-inserted generation and therefore exercises only reconciliation cleanup, not this first-insert path.

Critical: The real prose-driven host still has no executable apply-outcome failure writer. It invokes `runner.py apply-outcome`, whose exception paths only return 1/2 without mutating loop-state; the protocol then says every non-zero mutation suppresses projection and merely tells the host to transition to ESCALATE. The recovered `apply_outcome_or_escalate()` logic is only a Python helper that reruns apply-outcome and is not exposed by `runner.py`, so the shell-driven path cannot reliably persist the failure generation—several phases such as PLAN_REVIEW and VAL_REVIEW do not even have a generic `failed` transition outcome. Thus the production host can retain the old phase and old queue generation despite the round-4 recovery claim.

Critical: The installed Autopilot runtime mirrors do not match the canonical implementation at this exact review checkout. `.agents/skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py` and the identical `.claude` mirror still omit `projection_labels` from submit/reconcile and instead perform post-transaction issue label/update/list cleanup at lines 99-146, while the canonical file passes exact labels into the PostgreSQL transaction and performs no client-side cleanup. Agents launched through either installed mirror therefore retain the round-4 N/N+1 race and can remove the newer canonical generation's labels, contradicting validation-report.md's mirror-parity claim.

Critical: `submit_task` is not an exact set-idempotent label repair despite D9 stating that both submit and reconcile clear owned labels from every noncanonical row inside the per-change transaction. On a same-generation replay, lines 83-92 select and relabel only the canonical row, then return success; they never clear `projection:autopilot-phase` from another row for the same change. Any pre-existing or externally introduced double-labelled stale row therefore survives ordinary submit replay and remains board-visible alongside the canonical row, while the adapter reports `status=ok`. Only the reconcile function contains the noncanonical cleanup.

Critical: Installed runtime mirrors still ship the pre-038 client-side label-repair adapter. Canonical `skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py:73-100` passes `projection_labels` into submit/reconcile and returns after `task_id` validation, but `.agents/skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py` and `.claude/skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py` omit `projection_labels` and then call `try_projection_issue_update` / `try_projection_issue_list` after the reconcile lock is released (mirror lines 74-146). Matching drift exists in `.agents`/`.claude` `coordination_bridge.py`, which lacks the `projection_labels` request field present in `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py:677-808`. SKILL.md documents `<skill-base-dir>` as typically `.claude/skills/autopilot/` or `.agents/skills/autopilot/` (`skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:407-408`), so coordinated hosts re-execute Round-4 consensus finding 3. Task 4.2 is checked done and validation claims mirror portability passed, but `skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py:104-112` only byte-compares `SKILL.md`, so script drift false-greens.

Critical: Migration 038 can stamp Autopilot projection labels onto a pre-existing non-`issue` row that already owns the projection key. `submit_task`/`reconcile_work_projection` validate incoming `p_task_type='issue'` when labels are present (`038_atomic_projection_labels.sql:50-56`, `:121-127`), but on `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` they select the existing key row and `UPDATE ... SET labels=p_projection_labels` with no `task_type='issue'` guard (`:84-92`, `:167-182`). Live suite still creates non-issue keyed rows (`test_work_queue_postgres.py:302-331`). Claim exclusion is `task_type <> 'issue'` (`037_autopilot_phase_projection_visibility.sql:25`) and `list_issues` filters `task_type=eq.issue` (`issue_service.py:314`), so the labelled row stays claimable and board-invisible while submit/reconcile report success.

Critical: The OpenAPI projection-label schema still accepts requests the runtime deterministically rejects. Both endpoints declare any two strings of at most 160 characters, and `/work/submit` permits those labels without a projection key and with any task_type; `_projection_labels_are_valid` instead requires a projection key, `task_type == "issue"`, the first item to equal `change:<projection_key.change_id>`, the second item to equal `projection:autopilot-phase`, and that exact order. A generated client can therefore send a schema-valid request and receive 422 `invalid_projection_labels`, so the claimed runtime/OpenAPI request-constraint parity is incomplete.

Nit: Prose-host auto `escalate_resume` authorization does not advance durable phase out of ESCALATE. `skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:125-127` states exit 3 means the resume was authorized and the run continues from `previous_phase`, but `runner.py` `_evaluate_gate` on `decision.proceed` only records/flushes and returns `EXIT_NO_PENDING_GATE` (`:169-171`) without `_apply_transition(..., "resolved")` or `enter_escalate` inverse. In-process `run_loop` applies the resolved edge after the gate (`autopilot.py` escalate-resume path), and interactive `gate-answer` applies edges (`runner.py:270-282`). An auto-disposition coordinated resume can therefore project and continue while `current_phase` remains ESCALATE.

Nit: `apply_outcome_or_escalate` remains a second ESCALATE writer that always bumps `total_iterations` and overwrites `previous_phase`, unlike `enter_escalate` which is idempotent when already escalated. `autopilot.py:670-672` unconditionally sets `previous_phase=phase`, `current_phase=ESCALATE`, and `total_iterations += 1`. A retry against an already-escalated loop-state double-advances the projection generation and can replace the original resume phase. Happy-path coverage only proves the first failure (`test_apply_outcome_contract.py:259-289`).

Optional: Same-generation reconcile/submit does not reactivate a terminal canonical row. After `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, 038 only relabels the existing id (`038_atomic_projection_labels.sql:167-182`) and never clears `cancelled`/`completed`/`failed` back to `pending`. If the head generation was cancelled out-of-band, reconcile reports success while `issue_service.py:319-321` hides cancelled rows from implicit label reads, so the board loses the current projection with no replacement insert.

Optional: OpenAPI declares `projection_labels.items.maxLength: 160` (`openspec/contracts/agent-coordinator/openapi/work-queue.yaml:102-106`, `:142-146`), but `WorkSubmitRequest`/`WorkReconcileRequest` only constrain list length 2 with bare `list[str]` items (`coordination_api.py:225`, `:236`). Exact-pair validation in `work_queue.py:255-267` makes this mostly latent, yet Round-4 claim that runtime and OpenAPI request constraints match is incomplete for per-item length.

none: Canonical ESCALATE recovery seams hold at HEAD. `_apply_transition` routes table ESCALATE edges through `enter_escalate` (`autopilot.py:827-832`), which records `previous_phase`, sets reason, and increments `total_iterations` once when leaving a non-ESCALATE phase (`:520-524`). Parametrized resume coverage is in `skills/tests/autopilot/test_phase_projection_runner.py:181-195`. Goal-gate refusal on `runner.py transition` persists ESCALATE and exits 0 (`runner.py:404-412`; test `:198-214`). `apply_outcome_or_escalate` persists failure history, bumps generation, and projects (`autopilot.py:651-681`; `test_apply_outcome_contract.py:259-289`).

none: Structured degraded projection cannot halt authoritative work. `runner.py project-state` writes the envelope and returns 0 for non-ok statuses (`:444-447`), covered by `test_phase_projection_runner.py:217-249`. SKILL protocol states degraded envelopes exit 0 so phase work continues (`SKILL.md:84-87`). Adapter `_degraded` never mutates LoopState (`queue_projection.py:28-34`, `:93-94`).

none: Canonical transactional label repair and cancelled-row board filtering are implemented and live-tested. Migration 038 holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock` then cancels/clears/labels inside one function (`038_atomic_projection_labels.sql:57-59`, `:128-182`). Concurrent N/N+1 coverage is in `test_work_queue_postgres.py:344-396`; three-generation replay/stale/claim exclusion in `test_autopilot_projection_acceptance_postgres.py:38-141`; >50 ordinary issues window in `:144-172`; connected EventBus/SSE current-only refresh in `:175-218`; FastAPI→PostgreSQL board path in `test_work_queue_live.py:28-74`. Implicit label-filtered reads exclude cancelled (`issue_service.py:319-321`; `test_issue_service.py:188-220`), and SSE snapshots use that path (`event_stream.py:180-184`).

none: Migration 038 preserves legacy non-projection submit/reconcile behavior and cannot select ordinary change-labelled issues for owned-label mutation. Unkeyed submit returns before the advisory lock (`038_atomic_projection_labels.sql:22-31`); NULL `p_projection_labels` skips label rewrite branches (`:90`, `:175`). Stale clear/repair predicates require `task_type='issue'`, complete projection identity, and `projection:autopilot-phase` (`:175-181`, `:189-195`). Legacy unkeyed HTTP submit remains covered by `test_work_queue_live.py:10-24`.

none: Coordinator-free tiers remain isolated from the new publisher. `autopilot.py`/`runner.py` have no top-level `queue_projection` import; `project-state` imports lazily (`runner.py:427-428`). SKILL limits projection to the coordinated tier (`SKILL.md:59-62`). AST and fail-fast transport spies cover D10 (`test_phase_projection_isolation.py:12-86`).

none: Generated architecture artifacts satisfy the freshness/provenance contract relative to producer input roots. `architecture.provenance.json` records `source_revision=04a51f68` (full refresh), `worktree_dirty=false`, `validation.status=passed`, and `input_roots` limited to migrations/src/kanban (`:135-176`). Commits after that refresh through HEAD `a8ba0a08` are documentation/validation only and do not alter those input roots; size alone is not treated as a defect.

none: File-derived resume projection is one-way and non-authoritative. `project-state` loads durable loop-state, derives `(change_id, phase, total_iterations)` only from that file, and leaves bytes unchanged (`test_phase_projection_runner.py:75-130`; adapter `queue_projection.py:52-66`, `:93-100`). Queue responses are not fed into state transitions.
